title: Yankees have questions despite ‘really good’ Ryan Weathers injury news
content:
Will Ryan Weathers pitch again for the New York Yankees this season? If he does, will the left-hander wind up in the bullpen by late September, which seemed the plan all along? And how will the Yankees cover the starting rotation in his absence?

The Yankees had answers to exactly zero of those questions Sunday morning before facing the Toronto Blue Jays at Yankee Stadium, despite learning late Saturday that they could hold out hope Weathers will return.

An MRI showed no structural damage to Weathers’ elbow or ulnar collateral ligament, and the flexor strain he suffered during an afternoon game Saturday was considered below a Grade 1, or very minor, the 26-year-old said. Still, the Yankees put him on the 15-day injured list and called up righty Brendan Beck to take his place on the roster.

“Big picture, obviously, really good news,” manager Aaron Boone said. “Try and let this thing calm down and hopefully get him back in some capacity before the end.”

Boone said the plan was for Weathers to not throw for two to four weeks. The manager added that the early prognosis was that there’s a “great chance” Weathers will pitch for the team in September and in the postseason.

But the Yankees have a couple of things to figure out.

It seems unlikely that Weathers would have time to build up as a starting pitcher before the playoffs if he’s shut down for as long as four weeks.

That might actually not be a bad thing.

The Yankees have monitored Weathers’ workload all year, and he’s already at 137 1/3 innings. That’s many more innings than he’s ever pitched in the majors in his six-year career. The Yankees may have been considering ways to scale back his usage to keep him fresh for October.

The problem: Weathers has been good, especially lately. Since June 18, he has a 2.71 ERA in 12 starts. The Yankees, just three games back of the first-place Tampa Bay Rays, still have a shot at the American League East crown. Every Weathers start would have been valuable.

A silver lining? Weathers said he wasn’t sure that he necessarily suffered the flexor strain pitching. In a conversation with The Athletic, he pointed to an awkward throw he made to first base fielding Ernie Clement’s fourth-inning bunt. Weathers said he felt something wrong in his forearm in the next at-bat against Daz Cameron. So, if he returns, the Yankees might have greater confidence he won’t reinjure himself pitching.

The Yankees have five off days the rest of the year, the first coming Monday. That works in their favor. They may be able to avoid using a fifth starter a couple of turns through the rotation.

Until then, the options to replace Weathers aren’t the most appealing. Beck (2.75 ERA, 22 starts) and righty prospect Elmer Rodríguez (2.75 ERA, 22 starts) have had good seasons at Triple-A Scranton/Wilkes-Barre. But neither has impressed in limited work in the majors.

“He’s been doing a good job, even pitching deep into some games down there,” Boone said of Rodríguez. “Him and Brendan Beck have both had really strong Triple-A seasons as starters for us down there. So they have earned the opportunity certainly to be in the conversation. Hopefully, if they get an opportunity, they can be a part of us winning games.”

The Yankees could also turn to righty Luis Gil as an opener option. They have been auditioning him in a relief role in the minors since he returned from shoulder inflammation Aug. 11. But the 2024 American League Rookie of the Year winner has plenty of experience starting.

The Yankees haven’t announced their starter for Tuesday’s home game against the Houston Astros. A bullpen game with lefty Ryan Yarbrough pitching in a bulk role could be an option.
